verses.text: All wisdom comes from the Lord
The sand of the sea, the drops of rain,
The height of heaven, the breadth of the earth,
Wisdom was created before all things,
The source of wisdom is God’s word in the highest heaven,
The root of wisdom—to whom has it been revealed?
The knowledge of wisdom—to whom was it manifested?
There is One who is wise, the Creator of all,
The Lord himself created wisdom in the holy spirit;
She dwells with all flesh according to his gift,
The fear of the Lord is glory and exultation,
The fear of the Lord delights the heart,
With him who fears the Lord it will go well at the end;
To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom;
She made among men an eternal foundation,
To fear the Lord is wisdom’s full measure;
she fills their whole house with desirable goods,
The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom,
He saw her and apportioned her;
To fear the Lord is the root of wisdom,
Unrighteous anger cannot be justified,
A patient man will endure until the right moment,
He will hide his words until the right moment,
In the treasuries of wisdom are wise sayings,
If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments,
For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction,
Do not disobey the fear of the Lord;
Be not a hypocrite in men’s sight,
Do not exalt yourself lest you fall,
My son, if you come forward to serve the Lord,
Set your heart right and be steadfast,
Await God’s patience, cling to him and do not depart,
Accept whatever is brought upon you,
For gold and silver are tested in the fire,
Trust in God, and he will help you;
You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy;
You who fear the Lord, trust in him,
you who fear the Lord, hope for good things,
Consider the ancient generations and see:
For the Lord is compassionate and merciful;
Woe to timid hearts and to slack hands,
Woe to the faint heart, for it has no trust!
Woe to you who have lost your endurance!
Those who fear the Lord will not disobey his words,
Those who fear the Lord will seek his approval,
Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts,
Let us fall into the hands of the Lord,
Listen to me your father, O children;
For the Lord honored the father above the children,
Whoever honors his father atones for sins,
and whoever glorifies his mother is like one who lays up treasure.
Whoever honors his father will be gladdened by his own children,
Whoever glorifies his father will have long life,
he will serve his parents as his masters.
Honor your father by word and deed,
For a father’s blessing strengthens the houses of the children,
Do not glorify yourself by dishonoring your father,
For a man’s glory comes from honoring his father,
O son, help your father in his old age,
even if he is lacking in understanding, show forbearance;
For kindness to a father will not be forgotten,
in the day of your affliction it will be remembered in your favor;
Whoever forsakes his father is like a blasphemer,
My son, perform your tasks in meekness;
The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself;
There are many who are noble and renowned,
For great is the might of the Lord;
Seek not what is too difficult for you,
Reflect upon what has been assigned to you,
Do not meddle in what is beyond your tasks,
For their hasty judgment has led many astray,
A stubborn mind will be afflicted at the end,
A stubborn mind will be burdened by troubles,
The affliction of the proud has no healing,
The mind of the wise man will ponder the words of the wise,
Water extinguishes a blazing fire:
Whoever repays favors gives thought to the future;
My son, deprive not the poor of his living,
Do not grieve the one who is hungry,
Do not add to the troubles of an angry mind,
Do not reject an afflicted suppliant,
Do not avert your eye from the needy,
for if in bitterness of soul he calls down a curse upon you,
Make yourself beloved in the congregation;
Incline your ear to the poor,
Deliver him who is wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer;
Be like a father to orphans,
Wisdom breathes life into her sons
Whoever loves her loves life,
Whoever holds her fast will obtain glory,
Those who serve her will minister to the Holy One;
He who obeys her will judge the nations,
If he has faith in her he will obtain her;
For she will walk with him in disguise,
Then she will come straight back to him and strengthen him,
But if he goes astray she will forsake him,
Observe the right time, and beware of evil;
For there is a shame which brings sin,
Do not show partiality, to your own harm,
Do not refrain from speaking at the crucial time,
For wisdom is known through speech,
Never speak against the truth,
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins,
Do not subject yourself to a foolish fellow,
Strive even to death for the truth
Do not be reckless in your speech,
Do not be like a lion in your home,
Let not your hand be extended to receive,
Do not set your heart on your wealth,
Do not follow your inclination and strength,
Do not say, “Who will have power over me?”
Do not say, “I sinned, and what happened to me?”
Do not be so confident of atonement
Do not say, “His mercy is great,
Do not delay to turn to the Lord,
Do not depend on dishonest wealth,
Do not winnow with every wind,
Be steadfast in your understanding,
Be quick to hear,
If you have understanding, answer your neighbor;
Glory and dishonor come from speaking,
Do not be called a slanderer,
In great or small matters do not act amiss,
for a bad name incurs shame and reproach:
Do not exalt yourself through your soul’s counsel,
You will devour your leaves and destroy your fruit,
An evil soul will destroy him who has it,
A pleasant voice multiplies friends and softens enemies,
Let those that are at peace with you be many,
When you gain a friend, gain him through testing,
For there is a friend who is such at his own convenience,
And there is a friend who changes into an enemy,
And there is a friend who is a table companion,
In prosperity he will make himself your equal,
but if you are brought low he will turn against you,
Keep yourself far from your enemies,
A faithful friend is a sturdy shelter:
There is nothing so precious as a faithful friend,
A faithful friend is an elixir of life;
Whoever fears the Lord directs his friendship aright,
My son, from your youth up choose instruction,
Come to her like one who plows and sows,
She seems very harsh to the uninstructed;
She will weigh him down like a heavy testing stone,
For wisdom is like her name,
Listen, my son, and accept my judgment;
Put your feet into her chains,
Put your shoulder under her and carry her,
Come to her with all your soul,
Search out and seek, and she will become known to you;
For at last you will find the rest she gives,
Then her chains will become for you a strong protection,
Her yoke is a golden ornament,
You will wear her like a glorious robe,
If you are willing, my son, you will be taught,
If you love to listen you will gain knowledge,
Stand in the assembly of the elders.
Be ready to listen to every narrative,
If you see an intelligent man, visit him early;
Do no evil, and evil will never befall you.
Stay away from wrong, and it will turn away from you.
My son, do not sow the furrows of injustice,
Do not seek from the Lord the highest office,
Do not assert your righteousness before the Lord,
Do not seek to become a judge,
Do not offend against the public,
Do not commit a sin twice;
Do not say, “He will consider the multitude of my gifts,
Do not be fainthearted in your prayer,
Do not ridicule a man who is bitter in soul,
Do not devise a lie against your brother,
Refuse to utter any lie,
Do not prattle in the assembly of the elders,
Do not hate toilsome labor,
Do not count yourself among the crowd of sinners;
Humble yourself greatly,
Do not exchange a friend for money,
Do not deprive yourself of a wise and good wife,
Do not abuse a servant who performs his work faithfully,
Let your soul love an intelligent servant;
Do you have cattle? Look after them;
Do you have children? Discipline them,
Do you have daughters? Be concerned for their chastity,
Give a daughter in marriage; you will have finished a great task.
If you have a wife who pleases you, do not cast her out;
With all your heart honor your father,
Remember that through your parents you were born;
With all your soul fear the Lord,
With all your might love your Maker,
Fear the Lord and honor the priest,
Stretch forth your hand to the poor,
Give graciously to all the living,
Do not fail those who weep,
Do not shrink from visiting a sick man,
In all you do, remember the end of your life,
Do not contend with a powerful man,
Do not quarrel with a rich man,
Do not argue with a chatterer,
Do not jest with an ill-bred person,
Do not reproach a man who is turning away from sin;
Do not disdain a man when he is old,
Do not rejoice over any one’s death;
Do not slight the discourse of the sages,
Do not disregard the discourse of the aged,
Do not kindle the coals of a sinner,
Do not get up and leave an insolent fellow,
Do not lend to a man who is stronger than you;
Do not give surety beyond your means,
Do not go to law against a judge,
Do not travel on the road with a foolhardy fellow,
Do not fight with a wrathful man,
Do not consult with a fool,
In the presence of a stranger do nothing that is to be kept secret,
Do not reveal your thoughts to every one,
Do not be jealous of the wife of your bosom,
Do not give yourself to a woman
Do not go to meet a loose woman,
Do not associate with a woman singer,
Do not look intently at a virgin,
Do not give yourself to harlots
Do not look around in the streets of a city,
Turn away your eyes from a shapely woman,
Never dine with another man’s wife,
Forsake not an old friend,
Do not envy the honors of a sinner,
Do not delight in what pleases the ungodly;
Keep far from a man who has the power to kill,
As much as you can, aim to know your neighbors,
Let your conversation be with men of understanding,
Let righteous men be your dinner companions,
A work will be praised for the skill of the craftsmen;
A babbler is feared in his city,
A wise magistrate will educate his people,
Like the magistrate of the people, so are his officials;
An undisciplined king will ruin his people,
The government of the earth is in the hands of the Lord,
The success of a man is in the hands of the Lord,
Do not be angry with your neighbor for any injury,
Arrogance is hateful before the Lord and before men,
Sovereignty passes from nation to nation
How can he who is dust and ashes be proud?
A long illness baffles the physician;
For when a man is dead,
The beginning of man’s pride is to depart from the Lord;
For the beginning of pride is sin,
The Lord has cast down the thrones of rulers,
The Lord has plucked up the roots of the nations,
The Lord has overthrown the lands of the nations,
He has removed some of them and destroyed them,
Pride was not created for men,
What race is worthy of honor? The human race.
Among brothers their leader is worthy of honor,
The rich, and the eminent, and the poor—
It is not right to despise an intelligent poor man,
The nobleman, and the judge, and the ruler will be honored,
Free men will be at the service of a wise servant,
Do not make a display of your wisdom when you do your work,
Better is a man who works and has an abundance of everything,
My son, glorify yourself with humility,
Who will justify the man that sins against himself?
A poor man is honored for his knowledge,
A man honored in poverty, how much more in wealth!
The wisdom of a humble man will lift up his head,
Do not praise a man for his good looks,
The bee is small among flying creatures,
Do not boast about wearing fine clothes,
Many kings have had to sit on the ground,
Many rulers have been greatly disgraced,
Do not find fault before you investigate;
Do not answer before you have heard,
Do not argue about a matter which does not concern you,
My son, do not busy yourself with many matters;
There is a man who works, and toils, and presses on,
There is another who is slow and needs help,
and raises up his head,
Good things and bad, life and death,
The gift of the Lord endures for those who are godly,
There is a man who is rich through his diligence and self-denial,
when he says, “I have found rest,
Stand by your covenant and attend to it,
Do not wonder at the works of a sinner,
The blessing of the Lord is the reward of the godly,
Do not say, “What do I need,
Do not say, “I have enough,
In the day of prosperity, adversity is forgotten,
For it is easy in the sight of the Lord
The misery of an hour makes one forget luxury,
Call no one happy before his death;
Do not bring every man into your home,
Like a decoy partridge in a cage, so is the mind of a proud man,
for he lies in wait, turning good into evil,
From a spark of fire come many burning coals,
Beware of a scoundrel, for he devises evil,
Receive a stranger into your home and he will upset you with commotion,
If you do a kindness, know to whom you do it,
Do good to a godly man, and you will be repaid—
No good will come to the man who persists in evil
Give to the godly man, but do not help the sinner.
Do good to the humble, but do not give to the ungodly;
For the Most High also hates sinners
Give to the good man, but do not help the sinner.
A friend will not be known in prosperity,
A man’s enemies are grieved when he prospers,
Never trust your enemy,
Even if he humbles himself and goes about cringing,
Do not put him next to you,
Who will pity a snake charmer bitten by a serpent,
So no one will pity a man who associates with a sinner
He will stay with you for a time,
An enemy will speak sweetly with his lips,
If calamity befalls you, you will find him there ahead of you;
he will shake his head, and clap his hands,
Whoever touches pitch will be defiled,
Do not lift a weight beyond your strength,
A rich man does wrong, and he even adds reproaches;
A rich man will exploit you if you can be of use to him,
If you own something, he will live with you;
When he needs you he will deceive you,
He will shame you with his foods,
Take care not to be led astray,
When a powerful man invites you, be reserved;
Do not push forward, lest you be repulsed;
Do not try to treat him as an equal,
Cruel is he who does not keep words to himself;
Keep words to yourself and be very watchful,
Every creature loves its like,
all living beings associate by species,
What fellowship has a wolf with a lamb?
What peace is there between a hyena and a dog?
Wild donkeys in the wilderness are the prey of lions;
Humility is an abomination to a proud man;
When a rich man totters, he is steadied by friends,
If a rich man slips, his helpers are many;
When the rich man speaks all are silent,
Riches are good if they are free from sin,
A man’s heart changes his countenance,
The mark of a happy heart is a cheerful face,
Blessed is the man who does not blunder with his lips
Blessed is he whose heart does not condemn him,
Riches are not seemly for a stingy man;
Whoever accumulates by depriving himself, accumulates for others;
If a man is mean to himself, to whom will he be generous?
No one is meaner than the man who is grudging to himself,
even if he does good, he does it unintentionally,
Evil is the man with a grudging eye;
A greedy man’s eye is not satisfied with a portion,
A stingy man’s eye begrudges bread,
My son, treat yourself well, according to your means,
Remember that death will not delay,
Do good to a friend before you die,
Do not deprive yourself of a happy day;
Will you not leave the fruit of your labors to another,
Give, and take, and beguile yourself,
All living beings become old like a garment,
Like flourishing leaves on a spreading tree
Every product decays and ceases to exist,
Blessed is the man who meditates on wisdom
He who reflects in his mind on her ways
Pursue wisdom like a hunter,
He who peers through her windows
he who encamps near her house
he will pitch his tent near her,
he will place his children under her shelter,
he will be sheltered by her from the heat,
The man who fears the Lord will do this,
She will come to meet him like a mother,
She will feed him with the bread of understanding,
He will lean on her and will not fall,
She will exalt him above his neighbors,
He will find gladness and a crown of rejoicing,
Foolish men will not obtain her,
She is far from men of pride,
A hymn of praise is not fitting on the lips of a sinner,
For a hymn of praise should be uttered in wisdom,
Do not say, “Because of the Lord I left the right way”;
Do not say, “It was he who led me astray”;
The Lord hates all abominations,
It was he who created man in the beginning,
If you will, you can keep the commandments, they will save you;
He has placed before you fire and water:
Before a man are life and death, good and evil,
For great is the wisdom of the Lord;
The eyes of the Lord are on those who fear him,
He has not commanded any one to be ungodly,
Do not desire a multitude of useless children,
If they multiply, do not rejoice in them,
Do not trust in their survival,
For through one man of understanding a city will be filled with people,
Many such things my eye has seen,
In an assembly of sinners a fire will be kindled,
He was not propitiated for the ancient giants
He did not spare the neighbors of Lot,
He showed no pity for a nation devoted to destruction,
nor for the six hundred thousand men on foot,
Even if there is only one stiffnecked person,
As great as his mercy, so great is also his reproof;
The sinner will not escape with his plunder,
He will make room for every act of mercy;
Do not say, “I shall be hidden from the Lord,
Behold, heaven and the highest heaven,
The mountains also and the foundations of the earth
And no mind will reflect on this.
Like a tempest which no man can see,
Who will announce his acts of justice?
This is what one devoid of understanding thinks;
Listen to me, my son, and acquire knowledge,
I will impart instruction by weight,
The works of the Lord have existed from the beginning by his creation,
He arranged his works in an eternal order,
They do not crowd one another aside,
After this the Lord looked upon the earth,
with all kinds of living beings he covered its surface,
The Lord created man out of earth,
he turned him back into earth again,
He gave to men few days, a limited time,
He placed the fear of them in all flesh,
He made for them discretion, with a tongue and eyes and ears;
He created in them the knowledge of the spirit;
He placed the fear of him into their hearts,
He made them glory in his wondrous deeds,
that they might praise his holy name,
He bestowed knowledge upon them,
He established with them an eternal covenant,
Their eyes saw his glorious majesty,
And he said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness.”
Their ways are always before him,
He appointed a ruler for every nation,
All their works are as the sun before him,
Their iniquities are not hidden from him,
A man’s almsgiving is like a signet with the Lord,
Afterward he will arise and repay them,
Yet to those who repent he grants a return,
Turn to the Lord and forsake your sins;
Return to the Most High and turn away from iniquity,
Who will sing praises to the Most High in Hades,
From the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving has ceased;
How great is the mercy of the Lord,
For all things cannot be in men,
What is brighter than the sun? Yet its light fails.
He marshals the host of the height of heaven;
He who lives for ever created the whole universe;
To none has he given power to proclaim his works;
Who can measure his majestic power?
It is not possible to diminish or increase them,
When a man has finished, he is just beginning,
What is man, and of what use is he?
The number of a man’s days is great if he reaches a hundred years.
Like a drop of water from the sea and a grain of sand
Therefore the Lord is patient with them
He sees and recognizes that their end will be evil;
The compassion of man is for his neighbor,
He has compassion on those who accept his discipline
My son, do not mix reproach with your good deeds,
Does not the dew assuage the scorching heat?
Indeed, does not a word surpass a good gift?
A fool is ungracious and abusive,
Before you speak, learn,
Before judgment, examine yourself,
Before falling ill, humble yourself,
Let nothing hinder you from paying a vow promptly,
Before making a vow, prepare yourself;
Think of his wrath on the day of death,
In the time of plenty think of the time of hunger;
From morning to evening conditions change,
A wise man is cautious in everything,
Every intelligent man knows wisdom,
Those who understand sayings become skilled themselves,
Do not follow your base desires,
If you allow your soul to take pleasure in base desire,
Do not revel in great luxury,
Do not become a beggar by feasting with borrowed money,
A workman who is a drunkard will not become rich;
Wine and women lead intelligent men astray,
Decay and worms will inherit him,
One who trusts others too quickly is lightminded,
One who rejoices in wickedness will be condemned,
and for one who hates gossip evil is lessened.
Never repeat a conversation,
With friend or foe do not report it,
for some one has heard you and watched you,
Have you heard a word? Let it die with you.
With such a word a fool will suffer pangs
Like an arrow stuck in the flesh of the thigh,
Question a friend, perhaps he did not do it;
Question a neighbor, perhaps he did not say it;
Question a friend, for often it is slander;
A person may make a slip without intending it.
Question your neighbor before you threaten him;
All wisdom is the fear of the Lord,
But the knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom,
There is a cleverness which is abominable,
Better is the God-fearing man who lacks intelligence,
There is a cleverness which is scrupulous but unjust,
There is a rascal bowed down in mourning,
He hides his face and pretends not to hear;
And if by lack of strength he is prevented from sinning,
A man is known by his appearance,
A man’s attire and open-mouthed laughter,
There is a reproof which is not timely;
How much better it is to reprove than to stay angry!
Like a eunuch’s desire to violate a maiden
There is one who by keeping silent is found wise,
There is one who keeps silent because he has no answer,
A wise man will be silent until the right moment,
Whoever uses too many words will be loathed,
There may be good fortune for a man in adversity,
There is a gift that profits you nothing,
There are losses because of glory,
There is a man who buys much for a little,
The wise man makes himself beloved through his words,
A fool’s gift will profit you nothing,
He gives little and upbraids much,
A fool will say, “I have no friend,
How many will ridicule him, and how often!
A slip on the pavement is better than a slip of the tongue;
An ungracious man is like a story told at the wrong time,
A proverb from a fool’s lips will be rejected,
A man may be prevented from sinning by his poverty,
A man may lose his life through shame,
A man may for shame make promises to a friend,
A lie is an ugly blot on a man;
A thief is preferable to a habitual liar,
The disposition of a liar brings disgrace,
He who speaks wisely will advance himself,
Whoever cultivates the soil will heap up his harvest,
Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise;
Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure,
Better is the man who hides his folly
Have you sinned, my son? Do so no more,
Flee from sin as from a snake;
All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword;
Terror and violence will lay waste riches;
The prayer of a poor man goes from his lips to the ears of God,
Whoever hates reproof walks in the steps of the sinner,
He who is mighty in speech is known from afar;
A man who builds his house with other people’s money
An assembly of the wicked is like tow gathered together,
The way of sinners is smoothly paved with stones,
Whoever keeps the law controls his thoughts,
He who is not clever cannot be taught,
The knowledge of a wise man will increase like a flood,
The mind of a fool is like a broken jar;
When a man of understanding hears a wise saying,
A fool’s narration is like a burden on a journey,
The utterance of a sensible man will be sought in the assembly,
Like a house that has vanished, so is wisdom to a fool;
To a senseless man education is chains on his feet,
A fool raises his voice when he laughs,
To a sensible man education is like a golden ornament,
The foot of a fool rushes into a house,
A boor peers into the house from the door,
It is ill-mannered for a man to listen at a door,
The lips of strangers will speak of these things,
The mind of fools is in their mouth,
When an ungodly man curses his adversary,
A whisperer defiles his own soul
The indolent may be compared to a filthy stone,
The indolent may be compared to the filth of dunghills;
It is a disgrace to be the father of an undisciplined son,
A sensible daughter obtains her husband,
An impudent daughter disgraces father and husband,
Like music in mourning is a tale told at the wrong time,
He who teaches a fool is like one who glues potsherds together,
He who tells a story to a fool tells it to a drowsy man;
Weep for the dead, for he lacks the light;
Mourning for the dead lasts seven days,
Do not talk much with a foolish man,
What is heavier than lead?
Sand, salt, and a piece of iron
A wooden beam firmly bonded into a building
A mind settled on an intelligent thought
Fences set on a high place
A man who pricks an eye will make tears fall,
One who throws a stone at birds scares them away,
Even if you have drawn your sword against a friend,
If you have opened your mouth against your friend,
Gain the trust of your neighbor in his poverty,
The vapor and smoke of the furnace precede the fire;
I will not be ashamed to protect a friend,
but if some harm should happen to me because of him,
O that a guard were set over my mouth,
O Lord, Father and Ruler of my life,
O that whips were set over my thoughts,
in order that my mistakes may not be multiplied,
O Lord, Father and God of my life,
and remove from me evil desire.
Let neither gluttony nor lust overcome me,
Listen, my children, to instruction concerning speech;
The sinner is overtaken through his lips,
Do not accustom your mouth to oaths,
for as a servant who is continually examined under torture
A man who swears many oaths will be filled with iniquity,
There is an utterance which is comparable to death;
Do not accustom your mouth to lewd vulgarity,
Remember your father and mother
A man accustomed to using insulting words
Two sorts of men multiply sins,
To a fornicator all bread tastes sweet;
A man who breaks his marriage vows
His fear is confined to the eyes of men,
Before the universe was created, it was known to him;
This man will be punished in the streets of the city,
So it is with a woman who leaves her husband
For first of all, she has disobeyed the law of the Most High;
She herself will be brought before the assembly,
Her children will not take root,
She will leave her memory for a curse,
Those who survive her will recognize
Wisdom will praise herself and is honored in God,
In the assembly of the Most High she will open her mouth,
“I came forth from the mouth of the Most High,
I dwelt in high places,
Alone I have made the circuit of the vault of heaven
In the waves of the sea, in the whole earth,
Among all these I sought a resting place;
“Then the Creator of all things gave me a commandment,
From eternity, in the beginning, he created me,
In the holy tabernacle I ministered before him,
In the beloved city likewise he gave me a resting place,
So I took root in an honored people,
“I grew tall like a cedar in Lebanon,
I grew tall like a palm tree in En-ge'di,
Like cassia and camel’s thorn I gave forth the aroma of spices,
Like a terebinth I spread out my branches,
Like a vine I caused loveliness to bud,
“Come to me, you who desire me,
For my teaching is sweeter than honey,
Those who eat me will hunger for more,
Whoever obeys me will not be put to shame,
All this is the book of the covenant of the Most High God,
It fills men with wisdom, like the Pi'shon,
It makes them full of understanding, like the Euphrates,
It makes instruction shine forth like light,
Just as the first man did not know her perfectly,
for her thought is more abundant than the sea,
I went forth like a canal from a river
I said, “I will water my orchard
I will again make instruction shine forth like the dawn,
I will again pour out teaching like prophecy,
Observe that I have not labored for myself alone,
My soul takes pleasure in three things,
My soul hates three kinds of men,
You have gathered nothing in your youth;
What an attractive thing is judgment in gray-haired men,
How attractive is wisdom in the aged,
Rich experience is the crown of the aged,
With nine thoughts I have gladdened my heart,
happy is he who lives with an intelligent wife,
happy is he who has gained good sense,
How great is he who has gained wisdom!
The fear of the Lord surpasses everything;
Any wound, but not a wound of the heart!
Any attack, but not an attack from those who hate!
There is no venom worse than a snake’s venom,
I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon
The wickedness of a wife changes her appearance,

A sandy ascent for the feet of the aged—
Do not be ensnared by a woman’s beauty,
There is wrath and impudence and great disgrace
A dejected mind, a gloomy face,
From a woman sin had its beginning,
Allow no outlet to water,
If she does not go as you direct,
Happy is the husband of a good wife;
A loyal wife rejoices her husband,
A good wife is a great blessing;
Whether rich or poor, his heart is glad,
Of three things my heart is afraid,
There is grief of heart and sorrow when a wife is envious of a rival,
An evil wife is an ox yoke which chafes;
There is great anger when a wife is drunken;
A wife’s harlotry shows in her lustful eyes,
Keep strict watch over a headstrong daughter,
Be on guard against her impudent eye,
As a thirsty wayfarer opens his mouth
A wife’s charm delights her husband,
A sensible and silent wife is a gift of the Lord,
A modest wife adds charm to charm,
Like the sun rising in the heights of the Lord,
Like the shining lamp on the holy lampstand,
Like pillars of gold on a base of silver,
At two things my heart is grieved,
A merchant can hardly keep from wrongdoing,
Many have committed sin for a trifle,
As a stake is driven firmly into a fissure between stones,
If a man is not steadfast and zealous in the fear of the Lord,
When a sieve is shaken, the refuse remains;
The kiln tests the potter’s vessels;
The fruit discloses the cultivation of a tree;
Do not praise a man before you hear him speak,
If you pursue justice, you will attain it
Birds flock with their kind;
A lion lies in wait for prey;
The talk of the godly man is always wise,

The talk of fools is offensive,
The talk of men given to swearing makes one’s hair stand on end,
The strife of the proud leads to bloodshed,
Whoever betrays secrets destroys confidence,
Love your friend and keep faith with him;
For as a man destroys his enemy,
And as you allow a bird to escape from your hand,
Do not go after him, for he is too far off,
For a wound may be bandaged,
Whoever winks his eye plans evil deeds,
In your presence his mouth is all sweetness,
I have hated many things, but none to be compared to him;
Whoever throws a stone straight up throws it on his own head;
He who digs a pit will fall into it,
If a man does evil, it will roll back upon him,
Mockery and abuse issue from the proud man,
Those who rejoice in the fall of the godly will be caught in a snare,
Anger and wrath, these also are abominations,
He that takes vengeance will suffer vengeance from the Lord,
Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done,
Does a man harbor anger against another,
Does he have no mercy toward a man like himself,
If he himself, being flesh, maintains wrath,
Remember the end of your life, and cease from enmity,
Remember the commandments, and do not be angry with your neighbor;
Refrain from strife, and you will lessen sins;
and a sinful man will disturb friends
In proportion to the fuel for the fire, so will be the burning,

If you blow on a spark, it will glow;
Curse the whisperer and deceiver,
Slander has shaken many,
Slander has driven away courageous women,
Whoever pays heed to slander will not find rest,
The blow of a whip raises a welt,
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword,
Happy is the man who is protected from it,
for its yoke is a yoke of iron,
its death is an evil death,

See that you fence in your property with thorns,
make balances and scales for your words,
Beware lest you err with your tongue,
He that shows mercy will lend to his neighbor,
Lend to your neighbor in the time of his need;
Confirm your word and keep faith with him,
Many persons regard a loan as a windfall,
A man will kiss another’s hands until he gets a loan,

Nevertheless, be patient with a man in humble circumstances,
Help a poor man for the commandment’s sake,

Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High,
Store up almsgiving in your treasury,
more than a mighty shield and more than a heavy spear,
A good man will be surety for his neighbor,

The sinner who has fallen into suretyship
Assist your neighbor according to your ability,
The essentials for life are water and bread

Be content with little or much.
It is a miserable life to go from house to house,
you will play the host and provide drink without being thanked,
“Come here, stranger, prepare the table,
“Give place, stranger, to an honored person;
These things are hard to bear for a man who has feeling:
He who loves his son will whip him often,
He who disciplines his son will profit by him,
He who teaches his son will make his enemies envious,
The father may die, and yet he is not dead,
while alive he saw and rejoiced,

A horse that is untamed turns out to be stubborn,
Pamper a child, and he will frighten you;
Do not laugh with him, lest you have sorrow with him,

Bow down his neck in his youth,
Discipline your son and take pains with him,
Better off is a poor man who is well and strong in constitution

There is no wealth better than health of body,

Good things poured out upon a mouth that is closed

he sees with his eyes and groans,
Do not give yourself over to sorrow,

Delight your soul and comfort your heart,

A man of cheerful and good heart

Wakeful anxiety prevents slumber,
The rich man toils as his wealth accumulates,
The poor man toils as his livelihood diminishes,
He who loves gold will not be justified,
Many have come to ruin because of gold,

Blessed is the rich man who is found blameless,
Who is he? And we will call him blessed,
Who has been tested by it and been found perfect?
His prosperity will be established,
Are you seated at the table of a great man?
Remember that a greedy eye is a bad thing.
Do not reach out your hand for everything you see,
Judge your neighbor’s feelings by your own,
Eat like a human being what is set before you,
Be the first to stop eating, for the sake of good manners,
If you are seated among many persons,
How ample a little is for a well-disciplined man!
Healthy sleep depends on moderate eating;
If you are overstuffed with food,
Listen to me, my son, and do not disregard me,
Men will praise the one who is liberal with food,
The city will complain of the one who is miserly with food,
Do not aim to be valiant over wine,
Fire and water prove the temper of steel,
Wine is like life to men,
Wine drunk in season and temperately
Wine drunk to excess is bitterness of soul,
Drunkenness increases the anger of a fool to his injury,
Do not reprove your neighbor at a banquet of wine,
If they make you master of the feast, do not exalt yourself;
when you have fulfilled your duties, take your place,
Speak, you who are older, for it is fitting that you should,
Where there is entertainment, do not pour out talk;
A ruby seal in a setting of gold
A seal of emerald in a rich setting of gold
Speak, young man, if there is need of you,
Speak concisely, say much in few words;
Among the great do not act as their equal;
Lightning speeds before the thunder,
Leave in good time and do not be the last;
Amuse yourself there, and do what you have in mind,
And for these things bless him who made you
He who fears the Lord will accept his discipline,
He who seeks the law will be filled with it,
Those who fear the Lord will form true judgments,
A sinful man will shun reproof,
A man of judgment will not overlook an idea,
Do nothing without deliberation;
Do not go on a path full of hazards,
Do not be overconfident on a smooth way,
and give good heed to your paths.
Guard yourself in every act,
He who believes the law gives heed to the commandments,
No evil will befall the man who fears the Lord,
A wise man will not hate the law,
A man of understanding will trust in the law;
Prepare what to say, and thus you will be heard;
The heart of a fool is like a cart wheel,
A stallion is like a mocking friend;
Why is any day better than another,
By the Lord’s decision they were distinguished,
some of them he exalted and hallowed,
All men are from the ground,
In the fulness of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them
some of them he blessed and exalted,
As clay in the hand of the potter—
Good is the opposite of evil,
Look upon all the works of the Most High;
I was the last on watch;
Consider that I have not labored for myself alone,
Hear me, you who are great among the people,
To son or wife, to brother or friend,
While you are still alive and have breath in you,
For it is better that your children should ask from you
Excel in all that you do;
At the time when you end the days of your life,
Fodder and a stick and burdens for a donkey;
Set your slave to work, and you will find rest;
Yoke and thong will bow the neck,
Put him to work, that he may not be idle,
Set him to work, as is fitting for him,
Do not act immoderately toward anybody,
If you have a servant, let him be as yourself,
If you have a servant, treat him as a brother,
A man of no understanding has vain and false hopes,
As one who catches at a shadow and pursues the wind,
The vision of dreams is this against that,
From an unclean thing what will be made clean?
Divinations and omens and dreams are folly,
Unless they are sent from the Most High as a visitation,
For dreams have deceived many,
Without such deceptions the law will be fulfilled,
An educated man knows many things,
He that is inexperienced knows few things,
I have seen many things in my travels,
I have often been in danger of death,
The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live,
He who fears the Lord will not be timid,
Blessed is the soul of the man who fears the Lord!
The eyes of the Lord are upon those who love him,
He lifts up the soul and gives light to the eyes;
If one sacrifices from what has been wrongfully obtained, the offering is blemished;
The Most High is not pleased with the offerings of the ungodly;
Like one who kills a son before his father’s eyes
The bread of the needy is the life of the poor;
To take away a neighbor’s living is to murder him;
When one builds and another tears down,
When one prays and another curses,
If a man washes after touching a dead body, and touches it again,
So if a man fasts for his sins,
He who keeps the law makes many offerings;
He who returns a kindness offers fine flour,
To keep from wickedness is pleasing to the Lord,
Do not appear before the Lord empty-handed,
for all these things are to be done because of the commandment.
The offering of a righteous man anoints the altar,
The sacrifice of a righteous man is acceptable,
Glorify the Lord generously,
With every gift show a cheerful face,
Give to the Most High as he has given,
For the Lord is the one who repays,
Do not offer him a bribe, for he will not accept it;
He will not show partiality in the case of a poor man;
He will not ignore the supplication of the fatherless,
Do not the tears of the widow run down her cheek
He whose service is pleasing to the Lord will be accepted,
The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds,
And the Lord will not delay,
till he repays man according to his deeds,
Mercy is as welcome when he afflicts them
Have mercy upon us, O Lord, the God of all, and look upon us,
send fear of you upon the nations.
Lift up your hand against foreign nations
As in us you have been sanctified before them,
and let them know you, as we have known
Show signs anew, and work further wonders;
Rouse your anger and pour out your wrath;
Hasten the day, and remember the appointed time,
Let him who survives be consumed in the fiery wrath,
Crush the heads of the rulers of the enemy,
Gather all the tribes of Jacob,
Have mercy, O Lord, upon the people called by your name,
Have pity on the city of your sanctuary,
Fill Zion with the celebration of your wondrous deeds,
Bear witness to those whom you created in the beginning,

Listen, O Lord, to the prayer of your servants,
The stomach will take any food,

A perverse mind will cause grief,
A woman will accept any man,
A woman’s beauty gladdens the countenance,

He who acquires a wife gets his best possession,
Where there is no fence, the property will be plundered;

Every friend will say, “I too am a friend”;
Is it not a grief to the death
O evil imagination, why were you formed

Do not forget a friend in your heart,
Every counselor praises counsel,

Do not consult with one who looks at you suspiciously;

And besides all this pray to the Most High
Reason is the beginning of every work,
As a clue to changes of heart
four turns of fortune appear,
A man may be shrewd and the teacher of many,

for grace was not given him by the Lord,
A man may be wise to his own advantage,
A wise man will instruct his own people,

The life of a man is numbered by days,

My son, test your soul while you live;
For not everything is good for every one,
Do not have an insatiable appetite for any luxury,
for overeating brings sickness,

Honor the physician with the honor due him, according to your need of him,
for healing comes from the Most High,

Was not water made sweet with a tree

the pharmacist makes of them a compound.
My son, when you are sick do not be negligent,

for they too will pray to the Lord
He who sins before his Maker,
My son, let your tears fall for the dead,

Do not give your heart to sorrow;
Do not forget, there is no coming back;
“Remember my doom, for yours is like it:
When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance cease,
The wisdom of the scribe depends on the opportunity of leisure;

So too is every craftsman and master workman

All these rely upon their hands,

On the other hand he who devotes himself
he will preserve the discourse of notable men

If the great Lord is willing,

if he lives long, he will leave a name greater than a thousand,
I have yet more to say, which I have thought upon,
Listen to me, O you holy sons,
send forth fragrance like frankincense,
ascribe majesty to his name
“All things are the works of the Lord, for they are very good,

His blessing covers the dry land like a river,

From the beginning good things were created for good people,
Basic to all the needs of man’s life

the teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions and vipers,

Their perplexities and fear of heart—

and how can you reject the good pleasure of the Most High?
The children of sinners are abominable children,

My children, observe instruction and be at peace;

of meddling with his maidservant—
of repeating and telling what you hear,

of profit from dealing with merchants,

while a virgin, lest she be defiled

I will now call to mind the works of the Lord,
The sun looks down on everything with its light,
The Lord has not enabled his holy ones

He declares what has been and what is to be,
No thought escapes him,
He has ordained the splendors of his wisdom,
How greatly to be desired are all his works,
All these things live and remain for ever

The pride of the heavenly heights is the clear firmament,

He made the moon also, to serve in its season

The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven,
At the command of the Holy One they stand as ordered,
Look upon the rainbow, and praise him who made it,

By his command he sends the driving snow
Therefore the storehouses are opened,
In his majesty he amasses the clouds,
At his appearing the mountains are shaken;
The voice of his thunder rebukes the earth;
The eye marvels at the beauty of its whiteness,
He pours the hoarfrost upon the earth like salt,

He consumes the mountains and burns up the wilderness,

Where shall we find strength to praise him?
Terrible is the Lord and very great,
When you praise the Lord, exalt him as much as you can;
Who has seen him and can describe him?
Many things greater than these lie hidden,
For the Lord has made all things,
Let us now praise famous men,
The Lord apportioned to them great glory,
There were those who ruled in their kingdoms,
leaders of the people in their deliberations
those who composed musical tunes,
rich men furnished with resources,
all these were honored in their generations,
There are some of them who have left a name,
And there are some who have no memorial,
But these were men of mercy,
their prosperity will remain with their descendants,
Their descendants stand by the covenants;
Their posterity will continue for ever,
Their bodies were buried in peace,
Peoples will declare their wisdom,
E'noch pleased the Lord, and was taken up;
Noah was found perfect and righteous;
Everlasting covenants were made with him

he kept the law of the Most High,

The blessing of all men and the covenant

He sanctified him through faithfulness and meekness;
He made him hear his voice,

He made an everlasting covenant with him,

with a holy garment, of gold and blue
with twisted scarlet, the work of a craftsman;
with a gold crown upon his turban,

His sacrifices shall be wholly burned
Moses ordained him,
He chose him out of all the living
In his commandments he gave him

for they eat the sacrifices to the Lord,
But in the land of the people he has no inheritance,
Phin'ehas the son of Elea'zar is the third in glory,

May the Lord grant you wisdom in your heart
Joshua the son of Nun was mighty in war,
How glorious he was when he lifted his hands
Who before him ever stood so firm?
Was not the sun held back by his hand?
He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One,
and the great Lord answered him
And in the days of Moses he did a loyal deed,
And these two alone were preserved
And the Lord gave Caleb strength,
so that all the sons of Israel might see
The judges also, with their respective names,
May their bones revive from where they lie,
Samuel, beloved by his Lord,
By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation,
By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet,

Then the Lord thundered from heaven,
and he wiped out the leaders of the people of Tyre

In his youth did he not kill a giant,
For he appealed to the Lord, the Most High,
So they glorified him for his ten thousands,
For he wiped out his enemies on every side,
In all that he did he gave thanks

He gave beauty to the feasts,
The Lord took away his sins,
After him rose up a wise son

How wise you became in your youth!
Your soul covered the earth,
Your name reached to far-off islands,
For your songs and proverbs and parables,
In the name of the Lord God,
But you laid your loins beside women,
You put stain upon your honor,
so that the sovereignty was divided
But the Lord will never give up his mercy,
Solomon rested with his fathers,

How glorious you were, O Eli'jah, in your wondrous deeds!
You who raised a corpse from death
who brought kings down to destruction,
who heard rebuke at Sinai
who anointed kings to inflict retribution,

you who are ready at the appointed time, it is written,
Blessed are those who saw you,
It was Eli'jah who was covered by the whirlwind,

As in his life he did wonders,

Some of them did what was pleasing to God,

For Hezeki'ah did what was pleasing to the Lord,
In his days the sun went backward,
By the spirit of might he saw the last things,
He revealed what was to occur to the end of time,
The memory of Josi'ah is like a blending of incense

Except David and Hezeki'ah and Josi'ah
for they gave their power to others,
who set fire to the chosen city of the sanctuary,

It was Ezek'iel who saw the vision of glory
For God remembered his enemies with storm,
May the bones of the twelve prophets
How shall we magnify Zerub'babel?
and so was Jesh'ua the son of Jo'zadak;
The memory of Nehemi'ah also is lasting;
No one like E'noch has been created on earth,
And no man like Joseph has been born,
Shem and Seth were honored among men,
The leader of his brethren and the pride of his people
He laid the foundations for the high double walls,

How glorious he was when the people gathered round him
Like the morning star among the clouds,
like the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High,
like roses in the days of the first fruits,
like fire and incense in the censer,
like an olive tree putting forth its fruit,
When he put on his glorious robe

all the sons of Aaron in their splendor
Finishing the service at the altars,
he reached out his hand to the cup
Then the sons of Aaron shouted,
Then all the people together made haste
And the singers praised him with their voices
And the people besought the Lord Most High
Then Simon came down, and lifted up his hands
and they bowed down in worship a second time,
And now bless the God of all,
May he give us gladness of heart,
that Israel may believe that the God of mercy is with us
With two nations my soul is vexed,
Those who live on Mount Se'ir, and the Philis'tines,
Instruction in understanding and knowledge
Blessed is he who concerns himself with these things,
For if he does them, he will be strong for all things,
I will give thanks to you, O Lord and King,
for you have been my protector and helper
and delivered me,
from choking fire on every side
from the depths of the belly of Hades,
the slander of an unrighteous tongue to the king.
They surrounded me on every side,
Then I remembered your mercy, O Lord,
And I sent up my supplication from the earth,
I appealed to the Lord, the Father of my lord,
I will praise your name continually,
for you saved me from destruction
While I was still young, before I went on my travels,
Before the temple I asked for her,
From blossom to ripening grape
I inclined my ear a little and received her,
I made progress therein;
For I resolved to live according to wisdom,
My soul grappled with wisdom,
I directed my soul to her,
My heart was stirred to seek her,
The Lord gave me a tongue as my reward,
Draw near to me, you who are untaught,
Why do you say you are lacking in these things,
I opened my mouth and said,
Put your neck under the yoke,
See with your eyes that I have labored little
Get instruction with a large sum of silver,
May your soul rejoice in his mercy,
Do your work before the appointed time,
